findings.claim: The new `exists()` guard keys on `e.sqlstate`, but the diff never attaches a `sqlstate` to the errors it raises, so `_NOT_THERE` can never match and `exists()` re-raises for an absent or unmigrated database instead of returning False.
findings.evidence: errors.py hunk `@@ -78,4 +78,9 @@` builds the error as `storage.DatabaseError(f"database error: {type(exc).__name__}" + (f" (SQLSTATE {sqlstate})" if sqlstate else ""))` — a message string only; the SQLSTATE is embedded in text, not set on the exception object (and the `psycopg.OperationalError` branch above it returns `storage.OperationalError("could not reach the Postgres database")` with no state at all, which is what a missing database (3D000) and a refused password both raise as). The `__init__.py` hunk then does `except storage.ERRORS as e: if getattr(e, "sqlstate", None) in _NOT_THERE: return False; raise`, so `getattr` returns `None` for every translated error and the function raises for `42P01`/`3D000`. Repair goal 3 requires "return False only when the database is absent or unmigrated"; this instead raises on an unmigrated database, regressing every caller that treats `exists() == False` as "not set up yet" (including `storage.exists`'s stated contract).
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the SQLSTATE on the translated error (e.g. `err = storage.DatabaseError(msg); err.sqlstate = sqlstate` in `errors.py`, or a `sqlstate` argument on `storage.DatabaseError`) and keep `_NOT_THERE` in sync with the branch that actually handles connection-time 3D000, so `exists()` can see it.

findings.claim: The new test asserts `getattr(raised.value, "sqlstate", None) == "22P02"` on a translated storage error that the diff never gives a `sqlstate` attribute, so the assertion fails wherever the test runs (and the whole module skips without test DSNs, so `tests-pass` would never notice).
findings.evidence: test line 38 `assert getattr(raised.value, "sqlstate", None) == "22P02"` vs errors.py hunk, which returns `storage.DatabaseError(f"database error: {type(exc).__name__}" + ...)` passing only the message; scope note requires judging "whether the new tests would fail on the old code" — this one instead fails on the *new* code (or never runs), so it does not validate the fix it is meant to protect.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert on the message contract the fix actually implements (no value leak, plus a fixed `SQLSTATE 22P02` substring), or set `sqlstate` on the raised error and assert that.

findings.claim: The diff changes user-visible error wording and `PostgresBackend.exists` semantics with no CHANGELOG.md or docs/*.md entry.
findings.evidence: Warning constraint `changelog-and-docs`: "CHANGELOG.md and the relevant docs/*.md are updated when behaviour changes." The diff replaces `message_primary`-based messages with `database error: <Class> (SQLSTATE …)`, changes `exists()` from returning False to raising, and moves the dashboard's `storage.exists` call into the error path; no changelog or docs file appears in the diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a CHANGELOG.md entry noting the new value-free error strings and the stricter `exists()` behaviour.
